text_original: Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Autohome's first test of the A6L 3.0T quattro flagship measured 0-100 km/h in 4.68 s and 80-120 km/h in 3.25 s, with strong, repeatable launches. Autohome measured 6.42 L/100 km over 212.8 km in eco mode and judges the 3.0T hybrid's consumption not excessive. Autohome measured 100-0 km/h braking at 35.11 m best and 35.6 m average over 10 runs with little fade. Autohome rates the A6L's 78.9 km/h moose-test result as strong for the class. Autohome notes the rear-wheel steering switches off in emergencies, so it only helps everyday agility, not evasive manoeuvres. Autohome found automated parking handled parallel and angled spaces efficiently but failed to recognise a dead-end space after repeated tries. Autohome finds the menu layout logical with common functions easy to reach and smooth map and menu transitions. Autohome states the voice assistant recognises speech accurately and understands intent well. Autohome states rear legroom is noticeably more generous than in the previous generation. Autohome notes cabin storage space is not especially generous.

Autohome's buying guide presents the 3.0T V6 flagship as the A6L's key advantage, since 5 Series and E-Class rivals at similar prices offer only 2.0T engines. Autohome's buying guide calls it a minor shortcoming that even the top 3.0T trim needs paid options for rear-wheel steering and air suspension.
